description: A trigger utility: a button and two inputs that fire a trigger and a gate, plus two outputs that either toggle between them or put out fresh random voltages

params.text: Fires the module once, as a rising edge at either input jack does
Sets the voltage the A output carries when it is the high one, or the range its random voltages cover, a whole number from 1 to 10
Sets the voltage the B output carries when it is the high one, or the range its random voltages cover, a whole number from 1 to 10
Sets the chance that an incoming trigger is acted on at all, 0 to 1
Sets a fixed gate length, 0.2 to 10 seconds; at 0 the gate follows the input instead
Chooses what the A and B outputs do: toggle between them at their voltage settings, or give each a fresh random voltage on every trigger, swinging either side of 0V or staying above it
Puts a random name from the maker's list into the label field, or clears it if one is already there

inputs.text: A rising edge fires the module; this jack and the one beside it are summed with the button, so any of the three will do it
A rising edge fires the module; this jack and the one beside it are summed with the button, so any of the three will do it

outputs.text: Carries a 1ms pulse at 10V each time a trigger is acted on
Carries a gate at 10V, either following the input or running for the fixed length set beside it
Carries the A voltage while A is the high one in toggle mode, or a fresh random voltage on every trigger in the two random modes
Carries the B voltage while A is the low one in toggle mode, or a fresh random voltage on every trigger in the two random modes

notes: the module comes up with A high and B at 0V
a polyphonic cable at either input is summed to one voltage before it is read
the text field at the bottom takes six characters of your own, for telling several copies of this module apart; it is not a control and clicking it gives no help
the Global Retrig menu item blocks retriggering when it is switched on, which is the opposite way round from what its name reads
the auto-name button draws from the first ten entries of a list of twenty-one, so eleven of the names can never come up
menu: Global Retrig — when this is switched on, a trigger arriving while a fixed-length gate is running is thrown away; switched off, every trigger is acted on
Add Slew to custom Gates — rounds the fixed-length gate into a fast attack and a slightly faster release instead of a square edge
Add Slew to random CV — slides the A and B outputs to each new random voltage instead of stepping, more slowly at wider range settings
Rnd::normal (default: uniform) — draws the random voltages from a bell-shaped spread clustered near the middle instead of an even one
